Facts: Heir brought division action mentioning lifetime donations to co-heirs; defendants appeared late and contested collation obligation, arguing no specific reduction request was made.
Legal Framework: Art. 737 Civil Code (collation obligation); Art. 553-564 Civil Code (reduction action); Art. 747-751 Civil Code (valuation for fictitious reunion).
Interpretative Issues: Whether collation arises automatically in division proceedings or requires specific request; how collation differs from reduction action; who bears burden of proving exemption from collation; how indirect donations should be valued.
Legal Principles: Collation arises automatically upon succession opening pursuant to Art. 737 Civil Code, unless expressly waived by deceased. Request for division mentioning donated assets as part of estate to be reconstructed suffices to trigger collation, without need for specific formal request. Party objecting to collation based on exemption bears burden of proof to all co-heirs. Unlike reduction (which renders infringing provision ineffective and allows legitimate heir to claim as third party), collation ensures balance among co-heirs by forming estate to be divided. Indirect donations must be valued at succession opening time with characteristics at purchase time. Late appearance of defendants affects reduction action only if legitimate portion infringement is ascertained, not collation obligation.
